title: Streak an agar plate in four quadrants with an inoculating loop, without gouging the agar
instruction: Streak the plate for isolated colonies: drag the loop through the drop and streak quadrant 1, then streak quadrants 2, 3 and 4 in turn, each starting with a few strokes back through the one before, without digging into the agar. Then put the loop in the discard tray.
context: Laboratory research automation: the four-quadrant streak is the standard way microbiology, clinical and research labs isolate a pure culture from a sample, done by hand many times a day (CDC 'Quadrant streaking for isolation' job aid; Sanders 2012, J. Vis. Exp. 63, e3064). The difficulty is physical: a slim loop held like a pen must glide its 4.5 mm ring over soft agar in long strokes with almost no force: lifted it draws nothing, pressed past about 0.25 N it tears the gel.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), same layout every trial. Agar plate: Fisherbrand FB0875712 polystyrene Petri dish base (100 x 15 mm style; 92 mm outside, 88 mm inside, 13.5 mm tall) holding 20 mL of set 1.5 % agar medium (e.g. LB agar), 3.3 mm deep, room temperature, no surface water; centred at (34.0, -6.0) on the table, lid off and set aside. Underside marked in black marker with a cross through the centre (one line along x, one along y) into quadrants 1 (far right, x > 0 and y < 0 from the plate's centre), 2 (far left), 3 (near left) and 4 (near right), numbered by 1-4 dots near the rim. Sample: a 10 uL drop of water tinted with blue food colouring, pipetted onto the agar in quadrant 1 just before the trial, 2.6 cm forward of and 1.1 cm right of the plate's centre. Loop: one sterile disposable 10 uL inoculating loop, polypropylene, 200 mm long, 3.6 mm handle, ring 4.5 mm across (MTC Bio M4025 or Heathrow Scientific 03-448-345), lying flat on the table along x with its ring towards the robot, ring centre at (20.2, -20.0), butt at (40.0, -20.0). Discard tray: autoclavable polypropylene tray, 25 x 18 cm, 4 cm deep, centred at (16.0, 5.0), long side along x.
scoring: From the trial video and a photo of the plate from above at the end; quadrants as marked; a streak is a line the loop's ring draws while resting on the agar. 0 if the agar is gouged anywhere (torn or cut into, seen in the photo) or a gripper touches the agar. 0.25: at least 40 mm of streak in quadrant 1, drawn through the drop. 0.5: and then at least 30 mm of streak in quadrant 2 with at least 2 strokes running back from quadrant 2 into quadrant 1. 0.75: and then quadrant 3 likewise (at least 30 mm, at least 2 strokes back into quadrant 2). 1.0: and then quadrant 4 likewise (at least 30 mm, at least 2 strokes back into quadrant 3, never touching quadrant 1), and the loop lying in the discard tray (all of it inside the tray's walls), let go, for 1 s. A quadrant streaked out of turn adds nothing. At most 0.25 if the loop returns to the drop after quadrant 1 is done; at most 0.75 until the loop lies in the discard tray and the gripper has let go of it.
reset_notes: A fresh marked agar plate with a new drop and a fresh loop for every trial (each plate and loop is single-use); empty the discard tray. The drop is pipetted just before the trial starts.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz. Dish and agar are fixed rigid bodies. The loop (listed size, 1.6 g) is a handle and, on a sprung hinge at the neck (0.1 N at the ring bends it about 3 mm), its neck and ring: the flexible polypropylene neck. The agar doesn't deform: a streak is recorded where the ring rests on it with at least 0.01 N, and a contact force over 0.25 N (agar gel strength over the ring's contact patch) counts as a gouge. The drop's liquid isn't simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,600 steps; the right arm turned towards the loop and the plate and hovered over them, but never grasped the loop; the left arm stayed near its start); demo: 1.0
